thread:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Elevated 5xx across API gateways for eu-west and us-west. Error spike started ~2995001000. Possible third-party edge CDN issue. Auto-alerting SRE oncall.

alice: seeing ~25% of requests returning TLS handshake failures + connection resets from EU pops. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/logger?query=5xx_eu (shared).

ben: confirmed from logs — client_conn reset + 'tls: bad certificate' from edge handshakes. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Severity P1 if sustained.

maria: checking external: Cloudflare status shows partial degradation in some POPs: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/xyz-incident (looks related).

kevin: rolling manual health check:
```
# quick TLS check to a few edge IPs we've seen fail
openssl s_client -connect 104.16.XX.XX:443 -servername api.redwood.com -brief
```
kevin: results show intermittent handshake timeouts and occasional cert mismatch responses (CN doesn't match SNI)

alice: impact matrix: public hosted API (free tier) heavy; Dedicated customers routed to reserved capacity mostly OK but some sessions via CF edge are erroring. Support queue getting 50% increase in tickets.

support-bot: created incident ticket INC-2978 and attached initial customer impact doc. Notifying account owners for Dedicated customers with high error rates.

ben: quick mitigations we can attempt now:
- Switch traffic for api.redwood.com subdomain to emergency origin route behind our ALB (bypass Cloudflare).
- Apply Cloudflare route failover to our secondary POP set (if available).
- Increase connection retries and short-circuit streaming to degrade gracefully.

maria: DNS TTL change to flip cname off CF -> propagation will be slow, not ideal. We have an internal proxy toggle that can be flipped faster.

alice: decision: flip internal proxy to bypass CF for EU and US-WEST traffic where handshake fails. Doing a canary first (5% traffic). Anyone object?

ben: no objections. I'll run the toggle and watch error rate.

kevin: pre-run checklist:
1) add traffic slice to canary (5%)
2) enable additional logging and keep old path for quick rollback
3) notify support and on-call pager

alice: executing now.

sre-bot: ACTION: canary toggle initiated by alice at 2995001205. Canary ID c-2026-47.

ben: canary in progress — deploying proxy toggle with route to origin via internal-eu-backend.

maria: metrics update: handshake errors drop from 25% -> 6% for the canary slice. Total 5xx reduced by ~12% so far.

alice: expand to 20% if stable for 3 mins.

kevin: expanding to 20% now. Observability: traces show increased latency on origin path (+30ms) but error rate lower.

support-bot: posting to customers: "We're investigating intermittent connectivity issues affecting reachability to our hosted API in some regions. Mitigation underway; updates every 30 min."

ben: after expanding to 20% we see aggregated error rate drop ~18%. Good signal.

alice: proceed to 60% over next 10 minutes, monitoring for edge-case failures. Keep rollback within 5 minutes if errors spike.

sre-bot: schedule: next checkpoint +5m (2995001370). Pager duty pinged for handoff.

kevin: heads-up: still seeing a subset of clients failing TLS on old CF path — likely misrouting at specific CF POPs. We'll need Cloudflare ticket with packet captures. Opening ticket now with CF support including sample IPs and s_client output.

maria: CF ticket opened: TICKET-67421. CF team responded: "investigating an internal config change impacting SNI routing in select POPs".

alice: current status: we've shifted ~65% traffic off CF edge in affected regions. Error rate overall down to ~4%. Dedicated customer fallbacks mostly stable.

ben: next actions:
- Keep canary expanded until CF confirms full rollback (TICKET-67421).
- Prepare post-incident RCA: root cause (CF SNI routing/config change) + our mitigations (internal proxy bypass) + customer communication draft.

kevin: note for RCA: capture timestamps, sample tcpdump + s_client logs, list affected POP IPs and ASNs, and all deployment toggles.

alice: I'll start the incident war room notes and assign action owners. Ben you own rollback plan, Maria owns CF comms liaison, Kevin owns logs + evidence.

support-bot: notified enterprise accounts: email sent to oncall-account-owners@redwood.com.

pager-duty: oncall handoff: night-shift (ben) to take lead at 2995001400. Alice will remain available for escalation.

ben: taking lead. Monitoring dashboard at https://internal.redwood/observability/incident/2995001111.

maria: CF just posted a partial fix to a subset of POPs — they're seeing improvements and will roll globally. We'll wait for their confirmation before fully rolling traffic back through CF.

alice: plan for customer-facing update in 30 mins: include what happened, who was impacted, what we did, and next steps/RCA ETA. Keep tone: transparent, avoiding blame.

kevin: capturing final logs for now. Putting a timestamped bundle under s3://redwood-incident-logs/2995001111/ for RCA.

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation active, error rates trending down. CF engagement open (TICKET-67421). Next update in 30m or on status change.

ben: leaving detailed runbook entry and toggles used in the incident channel for follow-up. We'll schedule a postmortem once CF confirms stable state and we've collected logs.

alice: thanks team. If anything spikes, @ben (oncall) escalate to me immediately.

support-bot: incident ticket INC-2978 updated with post-customer-note placeholder and list of affected customers.

maria: CF finally confirms global rollback at 2995001455: "root cause: erroneous routing config push affecting SNI routing on some POPs; rolling rollback completed."

kevin: re-enable normal routing gradually. I'll start re-routing 25% back to CF and observe TLS success.

ben: re-route complete. Final check: 5xx back to baseline (~0.5%). Closing active mitigations.

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rates returned to normal. Incident classification: third-party CDN edge routing/SNI config change. RCA owner: maria. Postmortem scheduled 24h.

alice: adding action items:
- Add automated SNI handshake synthetic checks across POPs.
- Improve emergency origin route playbook for faster switch with verified health checks.
- Update support templates.

maria: will draft RCA and include timeline, CF ticket, evidence bundle, and follow-ups.

ben: thanks all. Closing thread but keeping logs preserved for the PM.
